Data & Platforms: Blume et al.'s travel times and origin-destination passenger flow data
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Expected Utility Maximization: This approach involves formulating optimization problems that account for uncertainties and time-dependent decaying effects on utility, as seen in the development of integer linear programming (ILP) models for single-drone multiple-task scheduling problems and disinformation interdiction in social networks.

Greedy Algorithm for Robustness: This method involves designing greedy algorithms to search for solutions exactly and heuristically, as demonstrated in the investigation of causal link failures and their impact on flow networks.

Mixed-Integer Linear Programming for Disinformation Mitigation: This approach involves formulating mixed-integer linear programming models to interdict the spread of disinformation in social networks and mitigate its impact on physical infrastructure networks.

Network Optimization for Infrastructure Protection: This involves using optimization techniques, such as ILP and greedy algorithms, to design and analyze flow networks and protect them against failures and disruptions.
Summary Description: Sridhar Radhakrishnan is a researcher with expertise in computer science, industrial and systems engineering, and reliability and safety. His work focuses on developing optimization models and algorithms to address complex problems in disaster management, crisis management, defense, and security risks. He has applied his expertise to various domains, including power systems, supply chain systems, transportation systems, and social media. His research aims to improve network robustness, flow network optimization, disinformation interdiction, and infrastructure protection. He has also explored the application of machine learning and artificial intelligence in these areas. His work has significant implications for public health, national security, and environmental sustainability.
